steps.what: Plan class projects, field trips and guest visits and confirm educational and practical arrangements
Check readiness and supervise activities, guiding students to learn from the experience

tasks.design: Keep experiential planning and supervision with the teacher, using existing communication and planning documents in {EMAIL} and {DOCS}. No new itinerary generator, automatic booking or digital readiness feed is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activities require real arrangements, permissions, supervision and educational judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication and planning resources remain adequate for this design.
tasks.still_hard: Judge readiness, manage changing conditions and connect experience to subject learning.
tasks.human_edge: Notice risks and help students interpret what they encounter.
tasks.altitude: Planning, readiness and supervision responsibility remain with the teacher.

evidence.claim: Experiential learning involves physical coordination and live supervision; generated plans alone do not remove those duties.

assumptions: Teacher confirms date, venue, participants and arrangements directly in s1, including manual capture into the plan; no free structured itinerary is assumed.
Families and administration provide required permissions through the existing process. Teacher checks actual evidence in s2; all checking remains counted.
Classroom activity drafting and report generation are separate views. No new application or process creates upkeep.
unknowns: Which permissions and supervision arrangements the school requires
research_questions: Which unresolved arrangements most often change an activity shortly before it begins?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+60=100. Liaison, planning, readiness checks, supervision and learning reflection retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend staff meetings and serve on committees

steps.what: Read staff meeting agendas and committee papers and prepare a contribution
Attend staff meetings and serve on committees through discussion and agreed commitments

tasks.design: Retain preparation and participation with the teacher using existing papers in {DOCS}. A summary may help locate information, but this design does not introduce one or claim it replaces reading, deliberation or required attendance.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task requires understanding decisions and contributing professional judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared papers support preparation without a new workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Weigh colleagues’ concerns and commit to feasible action.
tasks.human_edge: Bring subject and classroom experience into school decisions.
tasks.altitude: Committee rights and attendance duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Explain a position with concrete classroom evidence

evidence.claim: Meeting participation and committee deliberation are not removed by making meeting documents searchable.

assumptions: Chair or secretary supplies existing agenda and papers; their production effort is unchanged outside focal labour.
Teacher reads and prepares in s1; no free structured decision brief is assumed.
Minute-taking and meeting administration are outside this task. No new system creates additional upkeep.
unknowns: Which committee decisions require the teacher’s participation
research_questions: Do participants receive decision papers early enough to prepare a useful contribution?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+70=100. Required preparation and attendance retain time; no hypothetical shorter meeting is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sponsor clubs, student organisations and contests

steps.what: Agree extracurricular activity plans, participants, dates and practical constraints with students
Record activity dates and participant updates in the shared extracurricular calendar
Sponsor and supervise activities and support student organisations and contest participation

tasks.design: Use an existing restricted {CALENDAR} and shared {DOCS} participant list as the single place for verified extracurricular arrangements. The teacher still agrees plans, captures updates and supervises activities; the change reduces copying dates between separate messages and lists.
tasks.previous_blocker: Date changes and participant updates may be copied across several informal lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native shared calendars can present one maintained schedule without an agent.
tasks.still_hard: Balance student initiative, access, permissions and practical supervision.
tasks.human_edge: Support participation and help students organise responsibly.
tasks.altitude: The teacher coordinates from a clearer schedule, with unchanged sponsorship responsibility.

reach.learn: Keep confirmed arrangements separate from proposals

evidence.claim: A single native shared calendar can reduce repeated schedule copying; the local time benefit is unmeasured.

assumptions: Teacher and students establish activity_id, date, time, room and agreed participation in s1; its full 30% remains. School administration confirms room availability through the existing process.
S2 remaining 9.75 units include first entry, checking student updates and manually resolving conflicts. Student input time is unchanged; no free structured availability feed is assumed.
Missing confirmations remain pending; no automatic room booking, public posting or family notification is introduced. Test the current calendar before configuring another view.
unknowns: Whether existing extracurricular arrangements already use a single calendar
Which participant details may be shared
research_questions: Does one calendar reduce repeated updates after capture and conflict checking are included?

already_counted.description: Capture arrangements and check changed dates and participants

incremental.description: Maintain calendar access and remove obsolete arrangements

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=30+9.75+55=94.75; gross=5.25%; minus 1 focal upkeep gives 4.25% net. Low: a single schedule already exists. High: only repeated schedule copying shrinks; planning, update capture and sponsorship retain effort.

tasks.short: Administer standardized tests and interpret results

steps.what: Prepare standardized ability and achievement tests under publisher instructions
Administer tests and record response collection and administration exceptions
Interpret authorised results to determine students’ strengths and needs with appropriate caveats
outputs: teacher interpretation of strengths and needs

tasks.design: Retain the prescribed test workflow in {OTHER}, the authorised assessment platform, and teacher interpretation of results. Native scoring already supplied by the test publisher remains existing infrastructure; no additional score model or placement automation is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test conditions and interpretation limits matter as much as obtaining a numerical result.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest’s open-answer scoring pilot does not establish suitability for a standardized test.
tasks.still_hard: Understand uncertainty and relate results to other evidence of learning.
tasks.human_edge: Avoid treating a score as a complete account of a pupil’s capability.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains administration and interpretation responsibility.

reach.task: Discuss strengths and needs indicated by test evidence
reach.learn: Use publisher interpretation guidance and administration caveats

evidence.claim: CheckMate suggests scores for open questions in a small teacher pilot; the digest does not claim approval for this standardized-test workflow.

assumptions: Test publisher or authorised scoring service produces scored results from collected responses under the existing contract; its effort is unchanged outside focal teacher labour.

Teacher checks pupil identity and arrangements in s1 and records exceptions in s2; no clean administration feed is assumed. Locally teacher-scored tests retain prescribed manual scoring with no claimed reduction.
The task excludes separate teacher-made test preparation covered elsewhere. No new tool or process creates incremental maintenance.
unknowns: Which test and interpretation rules the school uses
research_questions: Do interpretations explicitly account for administration exceptions and publisher limitations?

incremental.description: No new scoring or interpretation technology

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=20+40+40=100. Existing publisher scoring creates no new human saving; preparation, administration and interpretation remain unchanged.
